subject: Temporary QoS bump request — surge cap and prorated true-up
messages:
From: Sandra Liu <sandra@cloudcrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@cloudcrest.com
Date: 2028-05-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary QoS bump for launch week — request

Hi Kimberly,

We're ramping up for a marketing-driven launch next Tuesday and expect a 3-5x spike in token consumption for ~36 hours. Can Redwood temporarily raise our QPS/headroom for that window? Our engineering lead asked for a short-proof path so we don't hit hard throttles — preferably a short-lived QoS bump or a soft cap switch.

Two questions up front:
- Can we get a temporary cap increase (N hours) without changing our committed tier?
- How will billing be handled for the overrun — prorated true-up, flat burst fee, or per-token overage?

Would appreciate any options and a quick estimate; I attached our expected traffic model.

Thanks,
Sandra
Sandra Liu
Head of Integrations, CloudCrest

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Liu <sandra@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QoS bump for launch week — request

Sandra — thanks for the details and the attachment (got the spike model). Short answer: yes, we can support a short-window QoS bump. Options we typically offer: 

1) Temporary burst window (recommended) — elevate quota for a defined window (hours), automatic rollback. Billing: prorated true-up for consumed tokens above committed quota at standard overage rate. No contract change required.

2) Short-term soft cap swap — we route to a higher-rate variant (slightly higher per-token rate) for the window. Useful if your SLA sensitivity > cost sensitivity.

3) Hybrid credit — we can apply a one-time burst credit (discount) on the overrun and cap your per-token exposure. This requires approval (small addendum).

I'm attaching a quick "burst_calculator.xlsx" with estimates based on your model. Rafael, can you confirm typical discounting range for option 3 and whether we can make a one-time concession for CC-DW-4728?

If this works, I'll draft a short addendum (1 page) that describes the window, cap, and billing mechanics so your finance team can sign quickly.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QoS bump for launch week — request

On Fri, May 11, 2028 at 11:02 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Rafael, can you confirm typical discounting range for option 3 and whether we can make a one-time concession for CC-DW-4728?

Kim — for a one-off addendum we can offer a 10–20% concession on the overrun portion depending on the risk window and whether CloudCrest will commit to a short follow-on pilot or expansion. For a 36-hour window and predictable traffic model, suggest we propose:

- 15% discount on token overrun charged above the committed tier
- Cap customer's exposure at 1.5x their committed monthly spend for the billing period (to avoid surprise)
- Require sign-off on a 1-page addendum; finance to approve by copy.

I will white-label the pricing lines and pre-fill an addendum. Ben, FYI — this will touch billing reconciliation next month.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sandra Liu <sandra@cloudcrest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@cloudcrest.com
Date: 2028-05-12T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QoS bump for launch week — request

Thanks — that sounds reasonable. Two quick asks:
1) Can you send the one-page addendum and an estimated dollar range for the overrun using the attached model? We'll need that for our procurement team to greenlight payment terms.
2) Do we get any SLA/priority routing guarantees during the window? Launch traffic is latency-sensitive.

If you can get the addendum in the next 24 hours we'll route to procurement.

Best,
Sandra

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Liu <sandra@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-13T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary QoS bump for launch week — request

Sandra — attaching the signed addendum stub (redwood_surge_addendum_20280511.pdf) and a concise estimate: with your modeled spike we estimate ~$14,800–$18,600 in incremental overage before discount. With the one-off 15% concession and the 1.5x exposure cap, the net incremental liability would be roughly $12,580–$15,810.

On SLA: we will prioritize routing to our dedicated burst pool for the 36-hour window which materially reduces tail latency. It's not a formal SLA change but operationally we guarantee best-effort priority routing and will monitor closely; we can also add a failure rollback policy to the addendum (auto-failover to the pre-spike model).

If that matches what CloudCrest needs, reply with approval and I'll route the addendum to finance for countersignature.

Attachments: redwood_surge_addendum_20280511.pdf (1-page), burst_calculator.xlsx (estimates)

—Kimberly
